clue.text: Possible milk supplier given chips by Scotsman, perhaps

parts.note: chips are fries, especially in American usage
Ian is a typically Scottish first name, so a Scotsman, perhaps

explanation.surface: A dairy supplier is handed a portion of chips by a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' signals that the definition is an example: a Friesian is one breed of dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Friesian is a black-and-white breed of dairy cow, one example of an animal that supplies milk.

clue.text: Destruction surrounding gear in warship

indicators.note: surrounding means going all around, so the word for destruction encloses the gear

parts.note: fate can mean ruin or destruction, as in to meet one's fate
rig means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: Wrecking a fighting ship that is full of equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of fast naval vessel, historically a sailing ship and now an escort warship.

clue.text: Edition of magazine for children

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single numbered edition of a periodical

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a children's magazine; 'for' is a link joining two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is both one printing of a periodical and the legal term for a person's offspring.

clue.text: Pretty sash adapted for dance in Scotland

indicators.note: adapted means altered to fit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pretty sash is altered to wear for a Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish folk dance, named after the valley of the river Spey.

clue.text: Good queen supporting a British nun

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed beneath, so the queen goes below the other letters

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was the popular nickname of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A kindly monarch props up a British nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess is Elizabeth I of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the female head of an abbey of nuns, so herself a nun of high rank.

clue.text: Reportedly crucial place for loading and unloading ships

definitions.text: place for loading and unloading ships

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is reported, said out loud, so the word for crucial is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: something crucial is key, as in a key factor

explanation.surface: A dockside is described, according to reports, as vital for shipping cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone wharf or landing stage beside water where vessels berth to load and discharge cargo.

clue.text: Ill-fated United Nations woman entertaining king

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding within, so the woman's name takes in the king

parts.note: Lucy is a woman's name
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A doomed UN official hosts a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlucky means dogged by misfortune or bad luck, the same as doomed or ill-starred.

clue.text: Part of Canada that inspires our country?

indicators.note: inspires is read literally as breathes in, so the country is taken inside the other word

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill
for a British setter our country is the UK

explanation.surface: A Canadian region asks whether it motivates Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' looks like 'motivates' but is read as 'in-spires', breathing in. The Yukon is a territory in north-west Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yukon is a territory in north-western Canada, one of the country's three northern territories.

clue.text: Impress popular writer

parts.note: something popular is in, in fashion
a scribe is a writer, especially one who copies manuscripts

explanation.surface: A well-loved author makes a strong impression on readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' looks like 'make an impression on someone', but here it means to stamp or engrave a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress can mean to stamp or carve a mark into a surface, which is what inscribing does.

clue.text: Criticism originally faced by the French king

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the next word, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of faced
la is French for 'the' (feminine)
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch has to face criticism from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is informal for strong adverse comment, originally anti-aircraft fire, so harsh disapproval.

clue.text: Bike patron misplaced — a situation at Wimbledon, maybe?

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cyclist sponsor has lost a bike at the tennis championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; 'maybe?' signals an example, since break points happen in any tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a break point is a moment when the receiver could win a game on the opponent's serve.

clue.text: Expert having tendency to conceal notes

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide something inside, so the musical notes sit within the other word

parts.note: apt means having a tendency, as in apt to forget
D and E are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A skilled person is inclined to hide their written notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept as a noun is a highly skilled person, a master or virtuoso in some field.

clue.text: Old Arab nomad partially relishes a race north

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A desert wanderer of old enjoys a race heading northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the name for the nomadic Arabs of the Syrian and Arabian deserts in late antiquity, later any Muslim.

clue.text: Cut out PE without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation letters are taken away

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A school drops gym lessons, going ahead without any dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the school subject of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to remove by cutting, as a surgeon takes out a growth.

clue.text: Ride round outskirts of Orpington in violent storm

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for ride goes around the other letters

parts.note: to cycle is to ride a bicycle

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of Orpington

explanation.surface: A bike ride around the edge of a suburb is caught in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpington is a town on the south-east edge of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a system of winds rotating around a low-pressure centre, a powerful tempest.

clue.text: Ravine identified by Tory touring a US state

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the Tory abbreviation wraps around the state

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
NY is the abbreviation for New York, a US state

explanation.surface: A gorge is pointed out by a Conservative on a trip through America.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, steep-sided gorge, a large ravine typically cut by a river.

clue.text: Like King Arthur's men, losing head regularly

indicators.note: losing head means dropping the first letter of the word

parts.note: King Arthur's men were the knights of the Round Table, so like them is knightly

explanation.surface: Arthurian warriors keep getting beheaded, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as part of the beheading story, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightly means happening every night, so on a recurring schedule.

clue.text: Crystalline compound I demonstrated?

parts.note: sat in means took part in a sit-in, a form of protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A chemist claims to have demonstrated a crystal substance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I SAT IN: a sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place, so to demonstrate is to sit in. The question mark warns of this twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is an orange-red crystalline organic substance used in making dyes such as indigo.

clue.text: Noblewoman initially devouring undercooked game

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: first letter of devouring
first letter of undercooked
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A titled lady starts eating game that has not been cooked through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat in this picture of dinner, but it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman holding the rank of duke or a duke's wife, so a noble lady.

clue.text: Energy shown by revellers at first in seedy bar

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first letter goes inside the bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter of revellers

explanation.surface: Partygoers show energy at the start of a night in a grubby bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means energy and determination, the urge to achieve things.

clue.text: Qualm about king's possible aircraft accident

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for qualm goes around the king

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp feeling, as in a pang of conscience, a qualm
R stands for Rex, Latin for king; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A monarch has misgivings about a possible plane crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a crash, of a car or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is RAF slang for a crash landing or bump, so a likely mishap for a plane.

clue.text: Neighbourhood accommodating new stadium

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the word for neighbourhood holds the letter inside

parts.note: an area is a district or neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A local district makes room for a newly built sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sports and spectacles, like a stadium.

clue.text: Devotional carving kept in attic once

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the answer is held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A religious carved figure was once stored up in the loft.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image used in worship, especially in Orthodox churches, often painted or carved.

clue.text: Jarring sound principally associated with Neptune's spear

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of sound
the trident is the three-pronged spear of Neptune, Roman god of the sea

explanation.surface: A grating noise comes mainly from the sea god's three-pronged weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jarring sound' reads as one phrase, but 'Jarring' alone is the definition and 'sound' gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, grating on the ear, so jarring.

clue.text: Carefully looked at fish, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means spoken out loud, so the fish's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Someone peered closely at a fish, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or scrutinise it closely, so eyed is past tense observation.

clue.text: Insecure shifting dunes at end of bay

indicators.note: shifting means moving around, so the letters are rearranged
end of means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of bay

explanation.surface: Sand hills moving at the edge of a bay make for unstable ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means not firmly fixed, liable to wobble or fall, so lacking security.
